correctness.rationale: A word in f and f^(-1) translates each directed chain by its signed exponent; |t|≥2 strictly reduces rank when any chain arrow exists, and t=0 gives a partial identity. Rank equality of two mutual generators then forces f or f^(-1). For pure cyclic support, equality of generated local cyclic subgroup yields exactly φ(m) generators. Chains of r labeled vertices contribute z^r and cycles z^r/r to the exponential formulas; maximum chain length subtraction and period-lcm divisor Möbius inversion give the boxed profile expressions. The rook count |I_n| and Q_n=n!∑(1/j!) bound the total deviation by e/[2(n+1)]. Literal inverse submonoid closure checked independently for n=0,…,4, while the proof treats all n.

final_claim: In the finite symmetric inverse monoid, a generator with a nontrivial chain has exactly two generators f,f^(-1) for its embedded inverse submonoid; if no nontrivial chain the fiber has φ(m) generators on a fixed support. Labeled chain-cycle EGFs give the full (h,m) profile counts and the fraction of distinct embedded monogenic inverse submonoids tends to 1/2 of the rook monoid with error ≤e/[2(n+1)].
